sentences.zh: 孫惠

translations.literal: Section heading: Sun Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui.

sentences.zh: 孫惠，字德施，吳國富陽人，吳豫章太守賁曾孫也。

translations.literal: Sun Hui, courtesy name Deshi, was a native of Fuyang in the state of Wu; he was a great-grandson of Ben, who had been Grand Administrator of Yuzhang under Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui, whose courtesy name was Deshi, came from Fuyang in the old state of Wu and was a great-grandson of Ben, the Yuzhang grand administrator who had served Wu.

sentences.zh: 父祖並仕吳。

translations.literal: His father and grandfather both held office in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Both his father and his grandfather had served the Wu regime.

sentences.zh: 惠口訥，好學有才識，州辟不就，寓居蕭沛之間。

translations.literal: Hui was slow of tongue, loved learning, and had talent and judgment; the province summoned him but he did not take office, and he lodged between Xiao and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He was awkward in speech but a devoted student, with real ability and insight. Though the provincial authorities tried to appoint him, he stayed out of office and lived for a time between Xiao and Pei.

sentences.zh: 永甯初，赴齊王冏義，討趙王倫，以功封晉興縣侯，辟大司馬戶曹掾，轉東曹屬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongning era, he answered Prince of Qi Jiong's call to righteous arms and campaigned against Prince of Zhao Lun; for merit he was enfeoffed marquis of Jinxing County, appointed clerk in the Revenue Bureau of the Minister of War, then transferred to a subordinate post in the eastern bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongning began, he joined Sima Jiong, the Prince of Qi, in the loyalist campaign against Sima Lun, the Prince of Zhao. His service earned him the county marquisate of Jinxing, a post as clerk in the minister of war's revenue office, and then a place on the eastern staff.

sentences.zh: 冏驕矜僭侈，天下失望。

translations.literal: Jiong was arrogant, boastful, presumptuous, and extravagant; all under Heaven were disappointed in him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong grew haughty and overbearing, overstepping his rank and spending on a princely scale until the empire had lost faith in him.

sentences.zh: 惠獻言於冏，諷以五難、四不可，勸令歸籓，辭甚切至。

translations.literal: Hui submitted advice to Jiong, using 'five difficulties' and 'four impossibilities' as indirect admonition, urging him to return to his fief; the wording was extremely blunt and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui laid before him a carefully framed remonstrance—the 'five difficulties' and 'four impossibilities'—urging him to withdraw to his princely domain. The tone was urgent and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 冏不納。

translations.literal: Jiong did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 惠懼罪，辭疾去。

translations.literal: Hui feared punishment, pleaded illness, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing reprisals, Sun Hui pleaded illness and slipped away.

sentences.zh: 頃之，冏果敗。

translations.literal: Before long, Jiong indeed was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jiong fell, exactly as he had warned.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎薦惠為大將軍參軍、領奮威將軍、白沙督。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengdu Ying recommended Hui as staff adviser to the grand general, concurrently General Who Rouses Might, and commander at Baisha.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying, the Prince of Chengdu, then recommended him as an adviser on the grand general's staff, with the concurrent titles of General Who Rouses Might and commander of the Baisha garrison.

sentences.zh: 是時，穎將征長沙王乂，以陸機為前鋒都督。

translations.literal: At this time Ying was about to campaign against Prince of Changsha Yi and appointed Lu Ji as commander of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was preparing to move against Sima Yi, the Prince of Changsha, and named Lu Ji to lead the van.

sentences.zh: 惠與機同鄉里，憂其致禍，勸機讓都督于王粹。

translations.literal: Hui was from the same home region as Ji; fearing that Ji would bring disaster on himself, he urged Ji to yield the commander's post to Wang Cui.
translations.idiomatic: As a townsman of Lu Ji, Sun Hui worried the appointment would destroy him and urged him to step aside in favor of Wang Cui.

sentences.zh: 及機兄弟被戮，惠甚傷恨之。

translations.literal: When Ji and his brothers were executed, Hui deeply grieved and resented it.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Ji and his brothers were put to death, Sun Hui mourned them bitterly.

sentences.zh: 時惠又擅殺穎牙門將梁俊，懼罪，因改姓名以遁。

translations.literal: At that time Hui had also on his own authority killed Liang Jun, a gate-guard general under Ying; fearing punishment, he changed his name and fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: He had already killed Liang Jun, one of Ying's gate generals, without orders. Dreading the consequences, he took a new identity and went into hiding.

sentences.zh: 後東海王越舉兵下邳，惠乃詭稱南嶽逸士秦秘之，以書幹越曰：

translations.literal: Later, when Prince of the Eastern Sea Yue raised troops at Xiapi, Hui falsely styled himself Qin Mizhi, a recluse of the Southern Marchmount, and sent a letter to lobby Yue, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Sima Yue, the Prince of the Eastern Sea, mobilized at Xiapi, Sun Hui invented the persona of Qin Mizhi, a hermit of the southern sacred peak, and addressed him in a long letter that began:

sentences.zh: 天禍晉國，遘茲厄運。

translations.literal: Heaven has scourged the Jin state; we have encountered this evil fate.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is punishing Jin; the dynasty has stumbled into mortal peril.

sentences.zh: 曆觀危亡，其萌有漸，枝葉先零，根株乃斃。

translations.literal: Reviewing instances of peril and ruin through the ages, their sprouting has a gradual course: the branches and leaves wither first, then the root and trunk die.
translations.idiomatic: History shows that collapse comes in stages: the twigs die first, and only then does the trunk give way.

sentences.zh: 伏惟明公資睿哲之才，應神武之略，承衰亂之餘，當傾險之運，側身昏讒之俗，局蹐凶諂之間。

translations.literal: I humbly reflect that you, enlightened lord, possess wise and penetrating talent, correspond to a divinely martial strategy, inherit the aftermath of decline and turmoil, face a time of overturning and peril, set your body amid benighted slander, and tread cramped between vicious flattery.
translations.idiomatic: You combine keen judgment with a soldier's grasp of power, yet you stand in the wreckage of civil war, in an age that could tip either way, hemmed in by sycophants and whispering malice.

sentences.zh: 執夷正立，則取疾奸佞；

translations.literal: If you hold to impartial uprightness, then you incur the hatred of the crafty and fawning.
translations.idiomatic: Stand straight, and the crooked courtiers turn on you.

sentences.zh: 抱忠懷直，則見害賊臣。

translations.literal: If you embrace loyalty and harbor uprightness, then you are harmed by treacherous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Show loyalty and candor, and venal officials will work your ruin.

sentences.zh: 餔糟非聖性所堪，苟免非英雄之節，是以感激於世，發憤忘身。

translations.literal: To swill the dregs is not what a sage nature can bear; to seek bare escape is not the integrity of a hero. Therefore you are stirred toward the age and rouse yourself, forgetting your person.
translations.idiomatic: Muddling along like the world is not for a man of your stamp, and mere self-preservation is beneath a leader. That is why you have thrown yourself into the crisis, moved by duty more than by safety.

sentences.zh: 抗辭金門，則謇諤之言顯；

translations.literal: If you raise your voice at the golden gates, then forthright remonstrance is displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Speak out at court, and honest counsel becomes visible for all to see.

sentences.zh: 扶翼皇家，則匡主之功著。

translations.literal: If you support and shelter the imperial house, then the achievement of rectifying the ruler is manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Uphold the throne, and your service to the sovereign will speak for itself.

sentences.zh: 事雖未集，大命有在。

translations.literal: Though the enterprise is not yet completed, the great mandate yet exists.
translations.idiomatic: The work is unfinished, but Heaven's mandate still rests where it belongs.

sentences.zh: 夫以漢祖之賢，猶有彭城之恥；

translations.literal: Even with the worthiness of Han's Founding Emperor, he still had the shame of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Even Liu Bang suffered the humiliation of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏武之能，亦有濮陽之失。

translations.literal: Even with the ability of Wei Martial Emperor, he still had the loss at Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, for all his genius, once took a hard defeat at Puyang.

sentences.zh: 孟明三退，終於致果；

translations.literal: Meng Ming thrice retreated, yet in the end achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Mingyao retreated again and again, yet in the end he triumphed.

sentences.zh: 勾踐喪眾，期於擒吳。

translations.literal: Gou Jian lost his hosts, yet aimed at capturing Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Jian lost his army yet still brought down Wu.

sentences.zh: 今明公名著天下，聲振九域，公族歸美，萬國宗賢。

translations.literal: Now your enlightened lordship's name is inscribed across the realm, your fame shakes the nine provinces, the ducal houses turn their praise toward you, and the myriad states honor your worth.
translations.idiomatic: Your name already fills the empire, your reputation shakes every quarter, the great clans look to you with admiration, and the regions acclaim your virtue.

sentences.zh: 加以四王齊聖，仁明篤友，急難之感，同獎王室，股肱爪牙，足相維持。

translations.literal: Moreover the four princes are together sagely, humane, enlightened, and staunch in friendship; in the urgency of shared hardship they jointly assist the royal house, and as thighs, arms, claws, and fangs they are enough to sustain one another.
translations.idiomatic: The four princes are men of true benevolence and clear judgment, bound by friendship as much as by kinship; in this emergency they are pulling together for the dynasty, each a pillar the others can lean on.

sentences.zh: 皇穹無親，惟德是輔，惡盈福謙，鬼神所贊。

translations.literal: High Heaven is not partial; it aids the virtuous. Evil fills its measure and good receives humility—this is what ghosts and spirits bless.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven favors no house forever; it crowns the worthy, cuts down the proud, and smiles on humility—spirits and gods watch the same scales.

sentences.zh: 以明公達存亡之符，察成敗之變，審所履之運，思天人之功，武視東夏之籓，龍躍海嵎之野。

translations.literal: Because you, enlightened lord, comprehend the signs of survival and perdition, discern the turns of success and failure, examine the course you tread, and ponder the work of Heaven and man, you may boldly survey the eastern domains' bulwarks and leap like a dragon along the sea's edge.
translations.idiomatic: You read the signs of rise and fall, weigh every shift in fortune, and know both Heaven's part and man's; look east to the loyal fiefs and to the coast where a dragon might take wing.

sentences.zh: 西諮河間，南結征鎮，東命勁吳銳卒之富，北有幽并率義之旅，宣喻青徐，啟示群王，旁收雄俊，廣延秀傑，糾合攜貳，明其賞信。

translations.literal: To the west consult the Prince of Hejian; to the south ally with the expeditionary commanders; to the east summon the sharp hosts and rich levies of mighty Wu; to the north you have You and Bing with hosts who hold to righteousness. Proclaim it in Qing and Xu, open the way to the host of princes, broadly gather stalwarts, widely extend welcome to the outstanding, bind those who waver, and make clear rewards and good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Secure the Hejian prince to your west, tie the southern commanderies to you, call on Wu's seasoned troops in the east, and count on the loyal levies of You and Bing in the north. Rally Qing and Xu, signal every prince, recruit every able sword, win over the undecided, and make your rewards and your word ironclad.

sentences.zh: 仰惟天子蒙塵鄴宮，外矯詔命，擅誅無辜，豺狼篡噬，其事無遠。

translations.literal: I look up to the fact that the Son of Heaven is in dust at Ye Palace, while outside, forged edicts are used to kill the guiltless; wolves and jackals usurp and devour—this affair is not distant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lies humbled at Ye while forged orders slaughter the innocent beyond the walls; jackals hold the palace gates. None of this is ancient history—it is happening now.

sentences.zh: 夫心火傾移，喪亂可必，太白橫流，兵家攸杖，歲鎮所去，天厭其德。

translations.literal: When the fire of the heart tilts and shifts, ruin is certain; when the Grand White sweeps across the sky, soldiers take their cue; where the year-star and the garrison star turn, Heaven tires of that virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The omens say it plainly: the throne's inner fire is guttering, the war star cuts the sky, and Heaven is withdrawing its mandate from the usurpers.

sentences.zh: 玄象著明，謫譴彰見。

translations.literal: The dark patterns are clear; reproof and warning shine forth.
translations.idiomatic: The constellations spell reproof; the warning could not be clearer.

sentences.zh: 違天不祥，奉時必克。

translations.literal: To oppose Heaven is inauspicious; to follow the season is sure to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Fight Heaven and you lose; move with the moment and victory follows.

sentences.zh: 明公思安危人神之應，慮禍敗前後之征，弘勞謙日昃之德，躬吐握求賢之義，傾府竭庫以振貧乏，將有濟世之才，渭濱之士，含奇謨於硃脣，握神策於玉掌，逍遙川嶽之上，以俟真人之求。

translations.literal: If you, enlightened lord, ponder the responses of men and spirits to safety and peril, consider the omens that foretell calamity and defeat, enlarge the virtue of toiling modestly from sun to sun, personally enact the righteousness of spitting out food and loosening hair to seek the worthy, empty the treasuries to relieve the destitute, then there will be talents who can save the age, men of the Wei River's banks, who hold strange plans behind vermilion lips and grasp divine stratagems in jade palms, roaming above rivers and peaks to await the true man's quest.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh how Heaven and the people answer danger and safety; read every warning written in defeat. Show the humility that keeps a ruler at his desk past dark, show the zeal that makes him skip meals to find advisers, open the granaries for the starving—and the strategists who can save the age, the sort once drawn from the banks of the Wei, will come: men who carry subtle plans behind a smile and a winning argument, who wait on mountain and river until the true leader calls.

sentences.zh: 目想不世之佐，耳聽非常之輔，舉而任之，則元勳建矣。

translations.literal: With your eyes you envision assistants not of a common age; with your ears you listen for extraordinary aides. Raise and employ them, then the founding merit is established.
translations.idiomatic: Picture in your mind's eye the rare counselor; listen for the voice that breaks the mold. Put such men in charge, and the great restoration is already half won.

sentences.zh: 秘之不天，值此衰運，竊慕墨翟、申包之誠，跋涉荊棘，重繭而至，櫛風沐雨，來承禍難。

translations.literal: I, Mizhi, am not favored by Heaven; I have met this declining fortune. Privately I admire the sincerity of Mo Di and Shen Bao, have trudged through brambles and come with soles layered from repeated blisters, combed the wind and washed in the rain, and come to undertake this calamitous hardship.
translations.idiomatic: I lack Heaven's favor and was born into a dying hour, yet I cherish the devotion of a Mo Di or a Shen Baoxu: I have crossed thorns until my feet were one blister, ridden wind and rain, and come to share this disaster with you.

sentences.zh: 思以管穴毗佐大猷，道險時吝，未敢自顯。

translations.literal: I wished to assist your great plan with my tube-and-hole perspective; the way is perilous and the times are mean, and I have not dared to reveal myself.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped my narrow view might still shore up your grand design, but the road is steep and the hour treacherous, so until now I have kept my name hidden.

sentences.zh: 伏在川泥，系情宸極，謹先白箋，以啟天慮。

translations.literal: I lie prostrate in river mud; my feelings cling to the polar throne. Respectfully I first present this note to open Heaven's consideration in you.
translations.idiomatic: I am nobody, mired far from court, yet my heart stays fixed on the throne. I send this paper first to lay my thoughts before you.

sentences.zh: 若猶沈吟際會，徘徊二端，徼幸在險，請從恕宥之例。

translations.literal: If you still hesitate at the conjunction of circumstances, waver between two courses, and hope for luck amid peril, I ask to follow the precedent that grants forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: If you linger between two paths, gambling on fortune in the teeth of danger, then treat my blunt words with the mercy you would show any petitioner who spoke out of turn.

sentences.zh: 明公今旋軫臣子之邦，宛轉名義之國，指麾則五嶽可傾，呼噏則江湖可竭。

translations.literal: You, enlightened lord, now turn your wheels in a land of ministers and sons, twist and turn within a realm of name and duty; a signal of your hand could tilt the five marchmounts, a breath could drain the rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: You ride through the heartland of loyal subjects, where every tie of name and duty runs through you alone. Lift a finger and the five sacred peaks tremble; draw breath and the great rivers could run dry.

sentences.zh: 況履順討逆，執正伐邪，是烏獲摧冰，賁育拉朽，猛獸吞狐，泰山壓卵，因風燎原，未足方也。

translations.literal: How much more when you tread the compliant to strike the rebellious, grasp the straight to attack the crooked—this is Wuhuo smashing ice, Ben and Yu tearing rotten wood, a fierce beast swallowing a fox, Mount Tai crushing an egg, or setting the plain ablaze with the wind; nothing matches it.
translations.idiomatic: What then of marching in the name of the right to crush rebellion, of wielding justice against treason? That is strength against weakness—Wuhuo shattering ice, legendary braves snapping rotten timber, a tiger swallowing a fox, Tai Shan grinding an egg, fire racing through dry grass under a gale.

sentences.zh: 今時至運集，天與神助，復不能鵲起于慶命之會，拔劍于時哉之機，恐流濫之禍不在一人。

translations.literal: Now the season arrives and fortune gathers; Heaven joins and spirits assist. If again you cannot rise like a magpie at the meeting of blessing's command, or draw your sword at the moment of the hour's chance, I fear the flood of disaster will not stop with one man.
translations.idiomatic: The moment and the mandate align; Heaven and the gods are offering their help. If you still fail to spring up when fortune calls or bare steel when the hour strikes, the coming deluge will drown more than a single life.

sentences.zh: 自先帝公王，海內名士，近者死亡，皆如蟲獸，屍元曳於糞壞，形骸捐於溝澗，非其口無忠貞之辭，心無義正之節，皆希目下之小生而惑終焉之大死。

translations.literal: From the former emperors and kings down to famous gentlemen within the seas, those lately dead have been like insects and beasts: corpses dragged in filth and mire, forms cast into ditches and gullies—not because their mouths lacked loyal language or their hearts lacked righteous uprightness, but all hoped for petty survival in the present eye and were deluded about the great death that ends everything.
translations.idiomatic: Late rulers and renowned scholars alike have died like animals—corpses hauled through filth, bones flung into ditches—not because they lacked loyal words or upright hearts, but because they clung to a little breathing space today and forgot the great finality waiting tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 凡人知友，猶有刎頸之報，朝廷之內，而無死命之臣。

translations.literal: Even among ordinary persons who are friends, there is still the repayment of severed-neck friendship; within the court there are none who pledge their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Common friends will die for one another, yet inside the palace no one will pledge his neck for the throne.

sentences.zh: 非獨秘之所恥，惜乎晉世之無人久矣。

translations.literal: It is not only that Mizhi is ashamed of this; I lament that the Jin age has long lacked such men.
translations.idiomatic: This shames me as much as it wounds the throne—for Jin has gone too long without men willing to die for it.

sentences.zh: 今天下喁喁，四海注目。

translations.literal: Now all under Heaven murmur; the four seas fix their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is holding its breath; every eye is on you.

sentences.zh: 社稷危而復安，宗廟替而復紹，惟明公兄弟能弘濟皇猷。

translations.literal: The altars of soil and grain were perilous and are restored to peace; the ancestral temples were replaced and are restored to continuation—only you, enlightened lord, and your brothers can broadly rescue the royal plan.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty tottered and may yet stand; the temples darkened and may yet see sacrifice again—only you and your brothers can carry the house of Sima through.

sentences.zh: 國之存亡，在斯舉矣。

translations.literal: Whether the state survives or perishes hangs on this one act.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom's life or death turns on what you do next.

sentences.zh: 秘之以下才之姿，而值危亂之運，竭其狗馬之節，加之忠貞之心，左屬平亂之鞬，右握滅逆之矢，控馬鵠立，計日俟命。

translations.literal: I, Mizhi, with the capacity of the lowest talent, yet meeting this time of peril and chaos, exhaust the fidelity of a dog or horse, add a heart of loyalty and uprightness, hang on my left the quiver that stills rebellion, grasp in my right the arrow that destroys traitors, rein in my horse and stand like a swan, counting the days while awaiting the command.
translations.idiomatic: I am the least of men, caught in the worst of seasons, yet I mean to spend myself like a loyal hound: loyal, upright, with a quiver for rebels on my left and a shaft for traitors in my right, holding my horse at the ready, counting the days until you give the word.

sentences.zh: 時難獲而易失，機速變而成禍，介如石焉，實無終日，自求多福，惟君裁之！

translations.literal: Times of hardship are hard to seize and easy to lose; opportunity speeds by and turns into calamity; firm as stone, in truth there is no whole day—seek your own abundant blessing; only you, lord, will decide!
translations.idiomatic: Crisis offers a narrow gate: hesitate and it slams shut, for fate moves faster than armies. I stand firm as stone but cannot wait forever; win your own blessing, my lord—the choice is yours alone.

sentences.zh: 越省書，榜道以求之，惠乃出見。

translations.literal: Yue read the letter and posted notices along the roads to seek him; Hui then came out to an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yue read the letter, put up notices on the highways to find the author, and Sun Hui at last came forward.

sentences.zh: 越即以為記室參軍，專職文疏，豫參謀議。

translations.literal: Yue immediately appointed him secretary on the staff, with sole charge of documents and drafts, and participation in planning and counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yue named him secretary-adviser on the spot, put him in charge of all memorials and proclamations, and brought him into every council of war.

sentences.zh: 除散騎郎、太子中庶子，復請補司空從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Palace and junior mentor to the heir apparent, then again requested appointment as assistant in the bureau of the minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as a palace gentleman and junior mentor to the crown prince, then asked to serve additionally as an aide in the minister of works' office.

sentences.zh: 越誅周穆等，夜召參軍王廙造表，廙戰懼，壞數紙不成。

translations.literal: When Yue executed Zhou Mu and others, he summoned at night the staff officer Wang Yi to draft the memorial; Yi trembled with fear and ruined several sheets of paper without completing it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue executed Zhou Mu's faction, he called Wang Yi in the dead of night to frame the rescript; Wang shook with fright and spoiled sheet after sheet without finishing.

sentences.zh: 時惠不在，越歎曰：「孫中郎在，表久就矣。

translations.literal: At that time Hui was not present. Yue sighed and said, 'Were Squadron Leader Sun here, the memorial would long since be finished.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui was away. Yue sighed, 'If Squadron Leader Sun were here, that document would already be done.'

sentences.zh: 」越遷太傅，以惠為軍諮祭酒，數諮訪得失。

translations.literal: ' Yue was promoted to grand tutor and appointed Hui as libationer-adviser on the army staff, repeatedly consulting him on gains and faults.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward Yue rose to grand tutor and made Sun Hui army libationer-adviser, consulting him constantly on what was sound and what was not.

sentences.zh: 每造書檄，越或驛馬催之，應命立成，皆有文采。

translations.literal: Whenever he produced letters or proclamations, Yue sometimes sent relay horses to hurry him; he answered the summons and completed them on the spot, and all had literary polish.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a dispatch was needed, Yue would sometimes put post riders on him to hurry the draft; Sun Hui produced polished prose on demand.

sentences.zh: 除秘書監，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed director of the palace library but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: They named him director of the palace library; he declined the post.

sentences.zh: 轉彭城內史、廣陵相，遷廣武將軍、安豐內史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to interior administrator of Pengcheng, administrator of Guangling, then promoted to General Who Spreads Might and interior administrator of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to interior administrator of Pengcheng and governor of Guangling, then rose to General Who Spreads Might and interior administrator of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 以迎大駕之功，封臨湘縣公。

translations.literal: For merit in welcoming the great chariot, he was enfeoffed duke of Linxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: His part in escorting the imperial carriage earned him the county dukedom of Linxiang.

sentences.zh: 元帝遣甘卓討周馥于壽陽，惠乃率眾應卓，馥敗走。

translations.literal: When the Yuan Emperor sent Gan Zhuo to campaign against Zhou Fu at Shouyang, Hui then led his hosts to join Zhuo; Fu was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan of Jin sent Gan Zhuo against Zhou Fu at Shouyang, Sun Hui brought his troops in on Gan's side; Zhou Fu broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 廬江何銳為安豐太守，惠權留郡境。

translations.literal: He Rui of Lujiang was interior administrator of Anfeng, and Hui for the time being retained control within the commandery borders.
translations.idiomatic: He Rui of Lujiang held the Anfeng magistracy while Sun Hui kept a temporary hold on the district.

sentences.zh: 銳以他事收惠下人推之，惠既非南朝所授，常慮讒間，因此大懼，遂攻殺銳，奔入蠻中。

translations.literal: Rui seized persons subordinate to Hui on another charge and pushed the case; Hui had not been appointed by the southern court and always feared slanderous estrangement; because of this he was greatly frightened, then attacked and killed Rui and fled into the Man tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He Rui arrested Sun Hui's followers on a trumped-up charge. Sun Hui had never received his post from the southern court and lived in fear of whispered accusations; panic drove him to strike first, kill He Rui, and bolt into Man country.

sentences.zh: 尋病卒，時年四十七。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and died at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 喪還鄉里，朝廷明其本心，追加吊賻。

translations.literal: When his funeral returned to his home region, the court, clarifying his original intent, added posthumous condolence gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When his body went home for burial, the court recognized what had truly moved him and sent additional mourning gifts.

sentences.zh: 熊遠

translations.literal: Section heading: Xiong Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan.

sentences.zh: 熊遠，字孝文，豫章南昌人也。

translations.literal: Xiong Yuan, courtesy name Xiaowen, was a native of Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan, courtesy name Xiaowen, came from Nanchang in Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖翹，嘗為石崇蒼頭，而性廉直，有士風。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiao had once been a menial of Shi Chong, yet was by nature honest and upright and had the bearing of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiong Qiao had once served Shi Chong as a household steward, yet remained honest and carried himself like a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎潘嶽見而稱異，勸崇免之，乃還鄉里。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue saw him and praised him as extraordinary, urged Chong to release him from servitude, and he then returned to his home region.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yue of the yellow gates noticed him, praised his quality, persuaded Shi Chong to free him, and he went home.

sentences.zh: 遠有志尚，縣召為功曹，不起，強與衣幘，扶之使謁。

translations.literal: Yuan had ambition and resolve; the county summoned him as merit clerk, but he would not rise; they forced on him cap and headcloth and supported him to make him go to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan had high aims. The county tried to name him merit clerk, but he refused to answer the call; they practically forced a cap on him and half carried him to the yamen.

sentences.zh: 十餘日薦於郡，由是辟為文學掾。

translations.literal: After more than ten days he was recommended to the commandery; thereby he was summoned as literary clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Within a fortnight the county had recommended him upward, and the commandery appointed him literary clerk.

sentences.zh: 遠曰：「辭大不辭小也。

translations.literal: Yuan said, 'One may decline a great post but not a small one.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan said, 'I may turn down a grand appointment, but not a humble one.'

sentences.zh: 」固請留縣。

translations.literal: ' He firmly requested to remain in the county.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted on staying at county level instead.

sentences.zh: 太守察遠孝廉。

translations.literal: The grand administrator nominated Yuan as filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: The grand administrator put him forward as filial and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 屬太守討氐羌，遠遂不行，送至隴右而還。

translations.literal: When the grand administrator campaigned against the Di and Qiang, Yuan then did not go, but escorted him to Longyou and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When that official marched against the Di and Qiang, Xiong Yuan declined to join the expedition but escorted him as far as Longyou before turning back.

sentences.zh: 後太守會稽夏靜辟為功曹。

translations.literal: Later the grand administrator Xia Jing of Kuaiji summoned him as merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xia Jing, grand administrator of Kuaiji, summoned him as merit clerk.

sentences.zh: 及靜去職，遠送至會稽以歸。

translations.literal: When Jing left office, Yuan escorted him to Kuaiji and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Jing left his post, Xiong Yuan saw him all the way to Kuaiji before heading home.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿、別駕，舉秀才，除監軍華軼司馬、領武昌太守、甯遠護軍。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as chief clerk and aide-de-camp, nominated him as flourishing talent, and appointed him aide to the supervising army Hua Yi, concurrently administrator of Wuchang and General Who Brings Peace from Afar.
translations.idiomatic: The province named him chief clerk and aide-de-camp, put him up as flourishing talent, and gave him staff posts under the supervising commander Hua Yi, with concurrent charge of Wuchang and the title General Who Brings Peace from Afar.

sentences.zh: 元帝作相，引為主簿。

translations.literal: When the Yuan Emperor was serving as minister, he brought Yuan in as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui was still minister, he took Xiong Yuan on as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時傳北陵被髮，帝將舉哀，遠上疏曰：「園陵既不親行，承傳言之者未可為定。

translations.literal: At that time a rumor spread that the northern mausoleum district had let its hair down in mourning; the emperor was about to observe mourning. Yuan submitted a memorial saying, 'As for the imperial tombs, since you have not gone in person, those who pass on hearsay cannot be taken as definitive.
translations.idiomatic: Word ran that mourners at the northern imperial tombs had loosened their hair in grief, and the prince was ready to go into full mourning. Xiong Yuan argued: you have not inspected the tombs yourself, so rumor is no basis for state ritual.'

sentences.zh: 且園陵非一，而直言侵犯，遠近吊問，答之宜當有主。

translations.literal: Moreover the tomb park is not one place; yet it is said outright that violation occurred. For condolences far and near, there ought to be a responsible authority in answering.
translations.idiomatic: The necropolis is not a single site; to speak flatly of 'violation' is premature. If the realm is to send condolences, someone must verify the facts before anyone replies.

sentences.zh: 謂應更遣使攝河南尹案行，得審問，然後可發哀。

translations.literal: I say you should further dispatch an envoy to act for the governor of Henan and conduct an inspection; after obtaining careful inquiry, then you may issue mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Send an acting governor of Henan to inspect the sites, establish the truth, and only then proclaim court mourning.

sentences.zh: 即宜命將至洛，修復園陵，討除逆類。

translations.literal: At once you should order a general to reach Luoyang, restore the tombs, and extirpate the rebellious sort.
translations.idiomatic: Order a general straight to Luoyang to repair the tombs and extirpate the usurpers.

sentences.zh: 昔宋殺無畏，莊王奮袂而起，衣冠相追於道，軍成宋城之下。

translations.literal: In olden times Song killed Wushe, and King Zhuang of Chu rolled up his sleeves and rose; caps and gowns followed one another on the road, and the army completed its deployment below Song's walls.
translations.idiomatic: When Song executed Wushe, King Zhuang of Chu sprang up, sleeves rolled, and officials thronged the roads until his host stood ready beneath Song's walls.

sentences.zh: 況此酷辱之大恥，臣子賓士之日！

translations.literal: How much more is this cruel outrage a great shame, a day when ministers and retainers should offer themselves!
translations.idiomatic: How much more is this shame—a moment when every loyal subject should stake life and station on the answer!

sentences.zh: 夫修園陵，至孝也；

translations.literal: To repair the imperial tombs is the utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Restoring the tombs is the highest filial duty.

sentences.zh: 討逆叛，至順也；

translations.literal: To punish the rebellious traitors is the utmost compliance with right.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing the traitors is perfect obedience to justice.

sentences.zh: 救社稷，至義也；

translations.literal: To rescue the altars of soil and grain is the utmost righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Saving the altars is the supreme righteous act.

sentences.zh: 恤遺黎，至仁也。

translations.literal: To show pity to the surviving people is the utmost benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Relieving the people who survive is the deepest humanity.

sentences.zh: 若修此四道，則天下回應，無思不服矣。

translations.literal: If you cultivate these four courses, then all under Heaven will turn in response, and none will fail to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Pursue those four policies and the realm will rally to you without a voice left outside your standard.

sentences.zh: 昔項羽殺義帝以為罪，漢祖哭之以為義，劉項存亡，在此一舉。

translations.literal: In olden times Xiang Yu killed the Righteous Emperor and took it as a crime, while Han's Founding Emperor wept over it and took it as righteousness; the survival of Liu and Xiang turned on this one act.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu murdered the Righteous Emperor and wore the guilt; Liu Bang mourned him and claimed the moral high ground—their struggle turned on that single gesture.

sentences.zh: 群賊豺狼，弱於往日；

translations.literal: The pack of rebels are jackals and wolves, yet weaker than in former days.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chiefs are wolves and jackals, and weaker now than before.

sentences.zh: 惡逆之甚，重於丘山。

translations.literal: The extremity of their villainy and treason weighs heavier than a hill or mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Their treason weighs heavier than any mountain.

sentences.zh: 大晉受命，未改於上；

translations.literal: The great Jin received the mandate; above, it has not yet altered.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin still holds the mandate; what sits above us has not changed.

sentences.zh: 兆庶謳吟，思德於下。

translations.literal: The myriad commoners sing and sigh, longing for virtue below.
translations.idiomatic: Among the people songs of longing rise; they hunger for true virtue from the throne.

sentences.zh: 今順天下之心，命貔貅之士，鳴檄前驅，大軍後至，威風赫然，聲振朔野，則上副西土義士之情，下允海內延頸之望矣。

translations.literal: Now go with the mind of all under Heaven, command bravo troops, sound the call to arms as the vanguard, let the great army follow after, awe-inspiring majesty blazing bright, fame shaking the northern wilds—then above you match the hearts of righteous men of the western lands, below you satisfy the hopes of all within the seas who crane their necks.
translations.idiomatic: March in accord with the realm's will: call up your bravest, let the drums of the van roll ahead, bring the main host behind in overwhelming force, and your name will thunder across the north—honoring the loyalists of the west and answering the yearning of everyone who watches for a sign.

sentences.zh: 」屬有杜弢之難，不能從。

translations.literal: Closing the memorial: but then there ensued the troubles of Du Tao, and he could not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ended there—but Du Tao's rebellion erupted, and the court could not act on his advice.

sentences.zh: 時江東草創，農桑弛廢，遠建議曰：「立春之日，天子祈穀于上帝，乃擇元辰，載耒耜，帥三公、九卿、諸侯、大夫，躬耕帝藉，以勸農功。

translations.literal: At the time the east of the Yang was newly founded, farming and sericulture were lax and abandoned. Yuan offered advice, saying: "On the day of Beginning of Spring the Son of Heaven prays for grain to High God, then selects an auspicious day, loads plow and handle, leads the Three Dukes, nine ministers, nobles, and grandees, and personally plows the imperial field to encourage agricultural labor.
translations.idiomatic: While the eastern court was still taking shape, fields lay idle and silk production had collapsed. Xiong Yuan urged: on Beginning of Spring the Son of Heaven prays to High God for the harvest, chooses a lucky day, takes up plow and share, leads the high ministers and nobles, and opens the sacred furrow himself to teach the realm the value of the soil.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：'弗躬弗親，庶人不信。

translations.literal: The Odes says, 'If he does not do it in his own person, the common people will not trust.'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes put it plainly: 'Unless the ruler goes himself, the people will not believe.'

sentences.zh: '自喪亂以來，農桑不修，遊食者多，皆由去本逐末故也。

translations.literal: ' Since the rebellions began, farming and sericulture have not been repaired; many roam seeking food—all because they have left the root and chased the tip.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, neither plough nor mulberry has been tended; idlers wander everywhere because men have abandoned the fundamentals for quick profit.

sentences.zh: 」時議美之。

translations.literal: When he had finished, discussion at the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When he set down his brush, the court praised his counsel.

sentences.zh: 建興初，正旦將作樂，遠諫曰；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianxing era, on New Year's Day they were about to perform music. Yuan remonstrated, saying;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianxing, when the court prepared music for New Year's Day, Xiong Yuan objected.

sentences.zh: 「謹案《尚書》，堯崩，四海遏密八音。

translations.literal: "I have examined the Documents: when Yao passed, within the four seas they cut off and silenced the eight kinds of music.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the Documents: when Yao died, music fell silent throughout the realm for the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 《禮》雲，凶年，天子撤樂減膳。

translations.literal: The Rites states: in a bad harvest year the Son of Heaven withdraws music and reduces meals.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites add that in famine years the Son of Heaven cancels performances and cuts his table.

sentences.zh: 孝懷皇帝梓宮未反，豺狼當途，人神同忿。

translations.literal: The late Emperor Xiaohuai's outer coffin has not returned; jackals and wolves block the road; men and spirits alike burn with anger.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai's catafalque still has not come home; jackals hold the road, and every man and god shares the outrage.

sentences.zh: 公明德茂親，社稷是賴。

translations.literal: You, sir, are of brilliant virtue and a luxuriant kinsman of the house; the altars of soil and grain rely on you.
translations.idiomatic: You combine moral weight with royal blood; the dynasty's survival rests on you.

sentences.zh: 今杜弢蟻聚湘川，比歲征行，百姓疲弊，故使義眾奉迎未舉。

translations.literal: Now Du Tao swarms like ants in the Xiang basin; year after year there have been campaigns, the hundred surnames are exhausted, therefore the righteous host that should welcome (the coffin) has not yet been able to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao still knots his forces along the Xiang; repeated campaigns have drained the people, so the loyal army that should escort the late emperor's remains has never mustered.

sentences.zh: 履端元日，正始之初，貢士鱗萃，南北雲集，有識之士於是觀禮。

translations.literal: On the first day that opens the year, at the beginning of the proper start, tribute scholars gather like scales, north and south cloud together—discerning men watch the ritual at this moment.
translations.idiomatic: New Year's Day opens the cycle; graduates crowd the capital like fish scales, coming from every quarter—and thoughtful men take the court's tone from what happens today.

sentences.zh: 公與國同體，憂容未歇。

translations.literal: You share one body with the state; mourning bearing has not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: You are the body of the state, and the mourning drum has hardly faded.

sentences.zh: 昔齊桓貫澤之會，有憂中國之心，不召而至者數國。

translations.literal: Formerly at Duke Huan of Qi's meeting at Guanze he had a mind anxious for the Central States, and without being summoned several states arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi once met the lords at Guanze with true worry for the heartland, and allies came unbidden.

sentences.zh: 及葵丘自矜，叛者九國。

translations.literal: When at Kuiqiu he grew arrogant, nine states rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When he strutted at Kuiqiu, nine states turned their backs.

sentences.zh: 人心所歸，惟道與義。

translations.literal: What human hearts turn to is only the Way and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts follow nothing but the Way and what is right.

sentences.zh: 將紹皇綱於既往，恢霸業於來今，表道德之軌，闡忠孝之儀，明仁義之統，弘禮樂之本，使四方之士退懷嘉則。

translations.literal: You will renew the imperial net for the past and enlarge hegemonic work for the present—display the track of virtue and power, clarify the model of loyalty and filial piety, make plain the bond of benevolence and righteousness, enlarge the root of rites and music, so that gentlemen from the four quarters withdraw carrying fine norms.
translations.idiomatic: You mean to mend what Heaven broke and build a lasting peace—show the path of true kingship, hold up loyalty and filial piety, bind the realm with benevolence and right, deepen rites and music, until every scholar who leaves your gate carries away a standard worth keeping.

sentences.zh: 今榮耳目之觀，崇戲弄之好，懼違《雲》、《韶》、《雅》、《頌》之美，非納軌物，有塵大教。

translations.literal: Now to glorify the eye's pleasure and exalt playful delights—I fear that would violate the beauty of Yun, Shao, Ya, and Song; it is not the accepting of standards and things, and would defile the great teaching.
translations.idiomatic: To dazzle the eye with spectacle and indulge in entertainments would betray the austere music of the classics; it would reject the very norms you claim to teach.

sentences.zh: 謂宜設饌以賜群下而已。

translations.literal: I judge it fit to set out a feast to grant the hosts below—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Lay a simple feast for your officials and stop there—that is enough for the day.

sentences.zh: 」元帝納之。

translations.literal: The Yuan Emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan of Jin took his advice.

sentences.zh: 轉丞相參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to staff adviser to the minister.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to a staff post under the minister.

sentences.zh: 是時琅邪國侍郎王鑒勸帝親征杜弢，遠又上疏曰：「皇綱失統，中夏多故，聖主肇祚，遠奉西都。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Jian, attendant gentleman of the Langye princedom, urged the emperor to campaign in person against Du Tao. Yuan again submitted a memorial saying: "The great net has lost its bond; the Central Plain has many troubles; the sagely lord has begun the enterprise and far respects the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, an attendant of the Langye princedom, pressed the throne to lead an expedition against Du Tao. Xiong Yuan added another memorial: the imperial order has frayed, the heartland is in chaos, yet your sagely enterprise still defers to the western capital.

sentences.zh: 梓宮外次，未反園陵，逆寇游魂，國賊未夷。

translations.literal: The outer coffin lies in temporary lodging; it has not returned to the tomb park; the wandering remnant of traitors—the national traitors are not yet pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's coffin still waits by the road; the tombs lie unrestored; rebel ghosts still roam, and the great traitors are unbeaten.

sentences.zh: 明公憂勞，乃心王室，伏讀聖教，人懷慷慨。

translations.literal: You, enlightened lord, labor with care; your heart is fixed on the royal house. Reading the sagely instruction, each man is moved to fervor.
translations.idiomatic: You wear yourself out for the house of Sima, and every man who reads your edicts burns to answer you.

sentences.zh: 杜弢小豎，寇抄湘川，比年征討，經載不夷。

translations.literal: Du Tao is a petty boy who raids and copies the Xiang basin; year after year there have been campaigns and punishments, yet for a full cycle he has not been pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao is a minor bandit chewing up the Xiang country; armies have marched against him year on year, yet he still stands after a full round of seasons.

sentences.zh: 昔高宗伐鬼方，三年乃克，用兵之難，非獨在今。

translations.literal: Formerly the High Ancestor campaigned against the Gui Fang and only after three years succeeded—the hardships of using troops are not only in the present.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu Ding needed three years to break the Gui Fang—war has always been slow work, not only today.

sentences.zh: 伏以古今之霸王遭時艱難，亦有親征以隆大勳，亦有遣將以平小寇。

translations.literal: I humbly reflect that through old and present, hegemons who met times of hardship sometimes campaigned in person to enlarge great merit, sometimes dispatched generals to pacify small bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Past and present, rulers in straits have either ridden east themselves to win lasting fame or sent a capable general to mop up a lesser foe.

sentences.zh: 今公親征，文武將吏、度支籌量、舟輿器械所出若足用者，然後可征。

translations.literal: Now if you, lord, campaign in person, if civil and military officers, commissary reckoning, boats, carts, and weapons produced are sufficient, only then may you campaign.
translations.idiomatic: A personal expedition demands ready generals, full supply lines, boats, carts, and arms—only when every piece is in place should you march.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜如前遣五千人，徑與水軍進征，既可得速，必不後時。

translations.literal: In my foolish opinion it is fitting, as before, to dispatch five thousand men to go straight with the water army on the expedition; then speed can be obtained and the season will certainly not be missed.
translations.idiomatic: Better, I think, to repeat the earlier plan: send five thousand men straight downriver with the fleet—fast, sure, and timely.

sentences.zh: 昔齊用穰苴，燕晉退軍；

translations.literal: Formerly when Qi employed Rang Ju, Yan and Jin withdrew their armies;
translations.idiomatic: When Qi put Tian Rangju in command, Yan and Jin broke off their siege.

sentences.zh: 秦用王翦，克平南荊。

translations.literal: when Qin employed Wang Jian, he was able to pacify southern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin gave Wang Jian the baton, he flattened the southern Jing.

sentences.zh: 必使督護得才，即賊不足慮也。

translations.literal: If you are sure to make the chief protector a man of talent, then the bandits are not worth worrying over."
translations.idiomatic: Name the right commander, and the bandits cease to matter.

sentences.zh: 」會弢已平，轉從事中郎，累遷太子中庶子、尚書左丞、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long Tao was already pacified; he was transferred to assistant in the bureau, and repeatedly promoted to junior mentor of the heir apparent, left vice-director of the ministry, and supernumerary gentleman attendant at court.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao fell before the plan was tested; Xiong Yuan was shifted to bureau assistant, then stepped up through junior mentor to the heir, left vice director of the ministry, and supernumerary gentleman at court.

sentences.zh: 帝每歎其忠公，謂曰：「卿在朝正色，不茹柔吐剛，忠亮至到，可為王臣也。

translations.literal: The emperor often praised his loyalty and fairness, saying to him, "In court you keep a straight countenance; you do not chew the soft and spit the hard; loyalty and candor reach the utmost—you may serve as the king's minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often praised his loyalty: 'You keep a straight face at court, neither bullying the weak nor truckling to the strong; your candor runs bone-deep—you are the stuff of kings' ministers.'

sentences.zh: 吾所欣賴，卿其勉之！」

translations.literal: What I delight in and rely on—do you strive in it!"
translations.idiomatic: You are where I place my trust—do not slacken.

sentences.zh: 及中興建，帝欲賜諸吏投刺勸進者加位一等，百姓投刺者賜司徒吏，凡二十餘萬。

translations.literal: When the restoration was established, the emperor wished to confer on all clerks who had presented their name-cards urging his advance one step in rank, and to grant commoners who had presented name-cards status as ministry clerks—in all more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration he wanted every clerk who had pressed a name card urging his accession raised a grade, and every commoner who had done the same enrolled as a ministry clerk—more than two hundred thousand people in all.

sentences.zh: 遠以為「秦漢因赦賜爵，非長制也。

translations.literal: Yuan held that "Qin and Han granted nobility by amnesty; that is not a lasting system."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan objected that Qin and Han had handed out titles with general amnesties—a policy that could not last.

sentences.zh: 今案投刺者不獨近者情重，遠者情輕，可依漢法例，賜天下爵，於恩為普，無偏頗之失。

translations.literal: Now consider that those who presented name-cards are not only such that the near have heavy feeling and the far have light feeling; in accordance with Han precedent you could grant nobility to all under Heaven—then favor would be universal, without the fault of partiality.
translations.idiomatic: The petitioners were not all equally close to you; better to follow Han practice and grant a general tithe of rank to the whole realm, spreading the favor evenly instead of picking favorites.

sentences.zh: 可以息檢核之煩，塞巧偽之端。

translations.literal: It can stop the vexation of checking and investigating and block the opening of trickery and pretense."
translations.idiomatic: That spares endless vetting and shuts the door on fraud.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear him.

sentences.zh: 轉御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 時尚書刁協用事，眾皆憚之。

translations.literal: At the time Director of the Ministry Diao Xie wielded power; all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie ran the ministry, and everyone walked wide of him.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎盧綝將入直，遇協于大司馬門外。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Ministry Lu Shen was about to go on watch and met Xie outside the great minister of war's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shen of the ministry was riding to his shift when he met Diao Xie outside the minister of war's gate.

sentences.zh: 協醉，使綝避之，綝不回。

translations.literal: Xie was drunk and had Shen give way; Shen would not turn back.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie, drunk, ordered Lu Shen to yield the road; Lu Shen refused to rein aside.

sentences.zh: 協令威儀牽捽綝墮馬，至協車前而後釋。

translations.literal: Xie ordered his guards of ceremony to drag Shen down from his horse and not release him until before Xie's carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie had his guards haul Lu Shen from the saddle and hold him kneeling before his own carriage.

sentences.zh: 遠奏免協官。

translations.literal: Yuan reported and had Xie dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan impeached Diao Xie and stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 時冬雷電，且大雨，帝下書責躬引過，遠復上疏曰：

translations.literal: At the time in winter there was thunder and lightning and moreover great rain; the emperor issued a document blaming himself and owning fault. Yuan again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: That winter brought thunder, lightning, and pounding rain; the emperor published a self-blaming edict, and Xiong Yuan answered with another memorial.

sentences.zh: 被庚午詔書，以雷電震，暴雨非時，深自克責。

translations.literal: I have received the gengwu edict, which because thunder and lightning shook (the palace) and violent rain came out of season deeply blames itself.
translations.idiomatic: I have read the gengwu edict blaming the court for untimely storm and lightning.

sentences.zh: 雖禹湯罪己，未足以喻。

translations.literal: Though Yu and Tang blamed themselves, it is not enough to compare.
translations.idiomatic: Even the self-reproach of Yu and Tang hardly matches your tone.

sentences.zh: 臣暗于天道，竊以人事論之。

translations.literal: I am dim about the way of Heaven; I dare discuss it by human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mind is dark to me; I speak only of what men have done.

sentences.zh: 陛下節儉敦朴，愷悌流惠，而王化未興者，皆群公卿士不能夙夜在公，以益大化，素餐負乘，秕穢明時之責也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is frugal and plain, kind and generous in spreading favor, yet kingly transformation has not risen—all because the host of dukes and ministers cannot from dawn to night attend to public duty so as to enlarge the great transformation; feasting on salary they bear the blame for riding high office while base, defiling the clear times.
translations.idiomatic: You live plainly and mean kindly by your people, yet good government does not take hold because your high ministers will not stay at their desks from dawn to dusk; they draw fat salaries while acting like petty men, smearing a moment that calls for clarity.

sentences.zh: 今逆賊猾夏，暴虐滋甚，二帝幽殯，梓宮未反，四海延頸，莫不東望。

translations.literal: Now the traitorous bandits toy with the Xia, cruelty and tyranny grow worse, the two emperors lie hidden in bier, the outer coffin has not returned; within the four seas they crane their necks, none not looking east.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels mock the heartland, cruelty deepens, two emperors lie unburied, the catafalque still wanders, and every corner of the realm cranes eastward for relief.

sentences.zh: 而未能遣軍北討，仇賊未報，此一失也。

translations.literal: Yet you have been unable to send the army north to campaign; the enemy is not avenged—this is one fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no host has gone north to avenge them—that is the first failure.

sentences.zh: 昔齊侯既敗，七年不飲酒食肉，況此恥尤大。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi after defeat seven years did not drink wine or eat meat—how much more is this shame greater.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi gave up meat and wine for seven years after a defeat; today's shame runs deeper still.

sentences.zh: 臣子之責，宜在枕戈為王前驅。

translations.literal: The duty of ministers and sons should be to pillow their spears and ride in the vanguard for the king.
translations.idiomatic: Subjects should sleep on their arms and ride ahead for their king.

sentences.zh: 若此志未果者，當上下克儉，恤人養士，撤樂減膳，惟修戎事。

translations.literal: If this resolve is not yet realized, then above and below should practice austerity and pity the people and nurture the men, withdraw music and reduce meals, and devote themselves solely to military matters.
translations.idiomatic: Until that can happen, court and country should tighten belts, cherish the people, feed the troops, cancel music, cut the kitchens, and think of nothing but war.

sentences.zh: 陛下憂勞于上，而群官未同戚容於下，每有會同，務在調戲酒食而已，此二失也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty toils above, yet the host of officers below do not share the bearing of grief; whenever there is a gathering, they strive only for jesting, wine, and food—this is the second fault.
translations.idiomatic: You mourn above while your officials feast below—every meeting turns to jokes, wine, and courses. That is the second failure.

sentences.zh: 選官用人，不料實德，惟在白望，不求才幹，鄉舉道廢，請托交行。

translations.literal: In selecting officials and employing men, they do not gauge true virtue, only look to empty reputation, do not seek practical ability; village nomination is abandoned, requests and pull-trading run rife.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments weigh swagger, not character, and pull never talent; the old village-recommendation path is dead, replaced by patronage and deals.

sentences.zh: 有德而無力者退，修望而有助者進；

translations.literal: Those with virtue but without power withdraw; those who cultivate reputation but have helpers advance;
translations.idiomatic: Men of quiet virtue fall back; well-connected mediocrities rise.

sentences.zh: 稱職以違俗見譏，虛資以從容見貴。

translations.literal: fitting the post yet departing from custom meets ridicule; empty pedigree yet moving at ease meets honor.
translations.idiomatic: Competence that offends fashion earns mockery; smooth drones with fine pedigrees win praise.

sentences.zh: 是故公正道虧，私途日開，強弱相陵，冤枉不理。

translations.literal: Therefore the path of fairness is damaged, private routes open day by day, strong and weak trample each other, and wrongs are not set right.
translations.idiomatic: Justice rots, backstairs thrive, bully grinds bully, and no wrong is righted.

sentences.zh: 今當官者以理事為俗吏，奉法為苛刻，盡禮為諂諛，從容為高妙，放蕩為達士，驕蹇為簡雅，此三失也。

translations.literal: Now those who hold office take attending to affairs as vulgar clerking, holding to law as harshness, exhausting ritual as flattery, ease and comfort as subtle excellence, license as being a thorough gentleman, arrogance as refined simplicity—this is the third fault.
translations.idiomatic: Officials now call diligence 'clerking,' law 'nitpicking,' courtesy 'flattery,' laziness 'sophistication,' debauch 'freedom,' and boorish pride 'ease.' That is the third failure.

sentences.zh: 世所謂三失者，公法加其身；

translations.literal: What the age calls three faults—public law applies to their persons;
translations.idiomatic: Men tagged with the 'three faults' face the full law.

sentences.zh: 私議貶其非；

translations.literal: private discussion demeans their wrongs;
translations.idiomatic: Gossip marks them for shame.

sentences.zh: 轉見排退，陸沈泥滓。

translations.literal: they are progressively pushed aside and sink into mud and mire.
translations.idiomatic: They are shoved aside and left to mire in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 時所謂三善者，王法所不加；

translations.literal: What the time calls three excellences—kingly law does not touch them;
translations.idiomatic: Men praised for the 'three excellences' never see the statute book.

sentences.zh: 清論美其賢；

translations.literal: pure discussion praises their worth;
translations.idiomatic: Pure chatter hails them as sages.

sentences.zh: 漸相登進，仕不輟官，攀龍附鳳，翱翔雲霄。

translations.literal: they are gradually promoted and advanced, serve without ceasing office, cling to dragon and attach to phoenix, and soar in the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: They climb without pause, clinging to every rising star until they ride the clouds.

sentences.zh: 遂使世人削方為圓，撓直為曲，豈待顧道德之清塗，踐仁義之區域乎！

translations.literal: Thereby the folk of the age shave squares into circles and bend straight into crooked—how then wait to look upon the clear path of virtue and tread the region of benevolence and righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: So the age files every square corner round and bends every straight line—who then still looks for the high road of virtue or the country of benevolence and right?

sentences.zh: 是以萬機未整，風俗偽薄，皆此之由。

translations.literal: Therefore the myriad threads of government are not ordered, customs are false and thin—all come from this.
translations.idiomatic: That is why government stays tangled and manners grow hollow.

sentences.zh: 不明其黜陟，以審能否，此則俗未可得而變也。

translations.literal: If one does not clarify their demotions and promotions so as to examine capability and inability, then customs cannot be obtained and changed.
translations.idiomatic: Until promotion and demotion honestly test talent, manners will not mend.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷群司以從順為善，相違見貶，不復論才之曲直，言之得失也。

translations.literal: Now the court host of offices takes compliance as good; mutual opposition meets demotion; they no longer debate whether talent is crooked or straight, whether speech hits or misses.
translations.idiomatic: Today the ministries reward yes-men and punish dissent; no one asks whether a man is crooked or straight, only whether he nods.

sentences.zh: 時有言者，或不見用，是以朝少辯爭之臣，士有祿仕之志焉。

translations.literal: At times there are speakers, yet sometimes they are not employed; therefore the court lacks disputing ministers, and gentlemen harbor the ambition of salary office alone.
translations.idiomatic: Even when someone speaks truth, he is ignored—so the hall has no debaters, and every scholar thinks only of keeping his stipend.

sentences.zh: 郭翼上書，武帝擢為屯留令，又置諫官，所以容受直言，誘進將來，故人得自盡，言無隱諱。

translations.literal: Gu Yi submitted a memorial, and Emperor Wu promoted him to magistrate of Tunliu; moreover he set up remonstrance officials in order to accept straight speech and draw forward the future, therefore each man could exhaust himself and words had no hidden reserve.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu Yi wrote bluntly, Emperor Wu made him magistrate of Tunliu and opened remonstrance posts so straight words had a door—men could speak their minds without fear.

sentences.zh: 任官然後爵之，位定然後祿之。

translations.literal: Appoint the office and then ennoble him; fix the rank and then grant salary.
translations.idiomatic: Give the post first, then the title; fix the grade, then the pay.

sentences.zh: 敷奏以言，明試以功，車服以庸。

translations.literal: Lay out plans in speech, test clearly by merit, grant chariots and robes according to achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Hear their plans, test them in deed, reward chariots and robes by proven work.

sentences.zh: 舜猶曆試諸難，而今先祿不試，甚違古義，亂之所由也。

translations.literal: Shun still was tried through many hardships; now first salary without trial greatly violates ancient meaning and is the source of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Even Shun was tried through ordeal; paying men before they prove themselves breaks the old pattern and breeds chaos.

sentences.zh: 求才急於疏賤，用刑先於親貴，然後令行禁止，野無遺滯。

translations.literal: Seek talent urgently from the distant and lowly, apply punishments first to the intimate and noble—only then will orders go and prohibitions stand, and the wilds have no stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: Hunt talent hard among the humble, swing the law first at the great—then orders bite, and nothing worthy languishes unseen.

sentences.zh: 堯取舜於仄陋，舜拔賢於岩穴，姬公不曲繩于天倫，叔向不虧法于孔懷。

translations.literal: Yao took Shun from a lowly corner; Shun raised worthies from rock caves; Duke Ji did not bend the cord for heavenly kin; Shu Xiang did not harm the law for close cousins.
translations.idiomatic: Yao drew Shun from obscurity, Shun from mountain caves; the Duke of Zhou did not bend law for kin, nor Shu Xiang for a brother's son.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷法吏多出於寒賤，是以章書日奏而不足以懲物，官人選才而不足以濟事。

translations.literal: Now the court's law clerks mostly come from cold and lowly (backgrounds); therefore memorials are submitted daily yet are not enough to correct things, and officials are selected for talent yet are not enough to accomplish tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Today your legal clerks rise from cold houses—papers flood in daily yet change nothing, and 'talent' fills the rolls yet nothing gets done.

sentences.zh: 宜招賢良于屠釣，聘耿介於丘園。

translations.literal: It is fitting to summon worthies from butchers and fishers and engage the upright from hills and gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Call up sages from butcher stalls and hermit huts alike.

sentences.zh: 若此道不改，雖並官省職，無救弊亂也。

translations.literal: If this way is not changed, though you double offices and cut posts, you cannot save the harm of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Without fixing that habit, merging bureaus will not cure the rot.

sentences.zh: 能哲而惠，何憂乎歡兜，何遷乎有苗，何畏乎巧言令色孔壬！

translations.literal: If one can be wise and kind, why worry about Huandou, why banish the Miao, why fear glib words, pleasing looks, and great craftiness!
translations.idiomatic: Be wise and kind, and who need fear Huandou, the Miao, or smooth-tongued courtiers?

sentences.zh: 此官得其人之益也。

translations.literal: This is the benefit of offices obtaining their proper men.
translations.idiomatic: That is what comes of putting the right man in each chair.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中，出補會稽內史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to attendant-in-ordinary, then went out to fill interior administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attendant-in-ordinary, then left the capital for Kuaiji as interior administrator.

sentences.zh: 時王敦作逆，沈充舉兵應之，加遠將軍，距而不受，不輸軍資於充，保境安眾為務。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Dun rebelled, Shen Chong raised troops in response; they added Yuan the title of general, but he resisted and would not accept, would not supply military funds to Chong, and made securing the border and calming the masses his task.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rose, Shen Chong answered him in arms; the court tried to name Xiong Yuan general, but he refused the baton, sent Shen Chong no supplies, and devoted himself to holding his territory quiet.

sentences.zh: 敦至石頭，諷朝廷征遠，乃拜太常卿，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Dun reached Stone Fortress he induced the court to summon Yuan; thereupon he was appointed grand master of ceremonies with supernumerary gentleman attendant at court.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Dun camped at Stone, he nudged the court into summoning Xiong Yuan away—so Yuan was given the grand master of ceremonies post with a supernumerary gentleman title.

sentences.zh: 敦深憚其正而有謀，引為長史。

translations.literal: Dun greatly feared his uprightness and strategizing and brought him in as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun feared his integrity and wit enough to pull him in as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 數月病卒。

translations.literal: After some months he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he died in office.

sentences.zh: 遠弟縉，名亞於遠，為王敦主簿，終於鄱陽太守。

translations.literal: Yuan's younger brother Xiong Jin, whose name ranked below Yuan's, was Wang Dun's chief clerk and ended as grand administrator of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiong Jin, less famous but still able, served Wang Dun as chief clerk and died as grand administrator of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 縉子鳴鵠，位至武昌太守。

translations.literal: Jin's son Minghu reached the office of grand administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's son Xiong Minghu rose to grand administrator of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 王鑒

translations.literal: Section heading: Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 王鑒，字茂高，堂邑人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jian, courtesy name Maogao, was a native of Tangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, courtesy name Maogao, came from Tangyi.

sentences.zh: 父濬，御史中丞。

translations.literal: His father Jun was palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Jun had been palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 鑒少以文筆著稱，初為元帝琅邪國侍郎。

translations.literal: Jian in youth was famed for literary brush; he first served as attendant gentleman of the Yuan Emperor's Langye princedom.
translations.idiomatic: He won early fame as a writer and began as an attendant gentleman when Yuan still held the Langye princedom.

sentences.zh: 時杜弢作逆，江湘流弊，王敦不能制，朝廷深以為憂。

translations.literal: At the time Du Tao rebelled, the Jiang and Xiang were flowing with harm; Wang Dun could not control it, and the court deeply took it as a worry.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Tao revolted, the Jiang and Xiang regions bled chaos that Wang Dun could not stifle, and the court grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 鑒上疏勸帝征之，曰：

translations.literal: Jian submitted a memorial urging the emperor to campaign against him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian urged the emperor to take the field himself, arguing:

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝深納之，即命中外戒嚴，將自征弢。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor deeply accepted it and at once ordered inner and outer vigilance, intending to campaign in person against Tao.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted every word, ordered full mobilization, and prepared to lead the host against Du Tao.

sentences.zh: 會弢已平，故止。

translations.literal: Before long Tao was already pacified, therefore it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao collapsed before the expedition sailed, so the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 中興建，拜駙馬都尉、奉朝請，出補永興令。

translations.literal: When the restoration was established, he was appointed commandant-escort and attendant at court, then went out to fill magistrate of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration he received the titles commandant-escort and court attendant, then took office as magistrate of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 大將軍王敦請為記室參軍，未就而卒，時年四十一。

translations.literal: Grand General Wang Dun requested him as secretary on the staff, but before he took up the post he died, aged forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun asked him onto his staff as secretary, but he died before he could report, at forty-one.

sentences.zh: 文集傳於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His literary collection survived him in circulation.

sentences.zh: 鑒弟濤及弟子戭，並有才筆。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Tao and his nephew Yan both had talent with the brush.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Wang Tao and his nephew Wang Yan were both fine writers.

sentences.zh: 濤字茂略，曆著作郎、無錫令。

translations.literal: Tao, courtesy name Maolue, successively served as editorial director and magistrate of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tao, courtesy Maolue, rose through editorial director to magistrate of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 戭字庭堅，亦為著作。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy name Tingjian, also served as editorial director.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, courtesy Tingjian, also held a compiler's post.

sentences.zh: 並早卒。

translations.literal: Both died early.
translations.idiomatic: Both died young.

sentences.zh: 陳頵

translations.literal: Section heading: Chen Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yun.

sentences.zh: 陳頵，字延思，陳國苦人也。

translations.literal: Chen Yun, courtesy name Yansi, was a native of Ku in the state of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yun, courtesy Yansi, came from Ku in the old state of Chen.

sentences.zh: 少好學，有文義。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and had literary judgment.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved books and showed a fine literary mind.

sentences.zh: 父訢立宅起門，頵曰：「當使容馬車。

translations.literal: When his father Xin built a house and raised the gate, Yun said, "It ought to allow room for a horse carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Xin built a new house and set the gate, Chen Yun said, 'Make it wide enough for a carriage.'

sentences.zh: 」訢笑而從之。

translations.literal: " Xin laughed and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: His father laughed—and widened the gate as he suggested.

sentences.zh: 仕為郡督郵，檢獲隱匿者三千人，為一州尤最。

translations.literal: He served as commandery postal inspector, investigated and seized three thousand persons in hiding, and was the foremost in one province.
translations.idiomatic: As commandery postal inspector he flushed out three thousand tax dodgers and ranked first in the province.

sentences.zh: 太守劉享拔為主簿，州辟部從事，乘馬車還家，宗党榮之。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Liu Xiang promoted him to chief clerk; the province summoned him as departmental retainer; he rode a horse carriage home, and his lineage and kin honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator Liu Xiang made him chief clerk, the province took him on as departmental retainer, and he rode home in a horse carriage to the pride of his clan.

sentences.zh: 劾案沛王韜獄，未竟，會解結代楊准為刺史，韜因河間王顒屬結。

translations.literal: He impeached and investigated the case of Prince of Pei's Tao; it was not finished when Xie Jie replaced Yang Zhun as inspector, and Tao through Prince of Hejian Yong importuned Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He was investigating Prince Pei's man Tao when Xie Jie replaced Yang Zhun as regional inspector; Tao then leaned on Sima Yong, the Prince of Hejian, to bring pressure on Xie Jie.

sentences.zh: 結至大會，問主簿史鳳曰：「沛王貴籓，州據何法而擅拘邪？

translations.literal: When Jie arrived he held a great assembly and asked chief clerk Shi Feng, "The Prince of Pei is a noble princedom—on what law of the province did you dare detain him without authority?
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Jie took up his post he called a full meeting and asked his chief clerk Shi Feng, 'The Prince of Pei is a royal fief—what statute let your office seize him on its own?'

sentences.zh: 」時頵在坐，對曰：「甲午詔書，刺史銜命，國之外台，其非所部而在境者，刺史並糾。

translations.literal: " At the time Yun was present and replied, "The jiawu-year edict: the inspector bears charge; beyond the capital he is the state's outer terrace; those who are not of his department but are within his borders—the inspector investigates them all.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yun, who was in the hall, answered: 'The jiawu edict made the inspector Heaven's agent beyond the capital: anyone inside his circuit, whether or not under his nominal department, falls under his remit.'

sentences.zh: 事征文墨，前後列上，七被詔書。

translations.literal: The affair is verified in documents; forward and backward it was listed and submitted, seven times receiving edict responses.
translations.idiomatic: The paperwork went up again and seven imperial replies confirmed the procedure.

sentences.zh: 如州所劾，無有違謬。

translations.literal: If it is as the province impeached, there is no violation or error.
translations.idiomatic: If the province's impeachment follows that paper trail, it is legally sound.

sentences.zh: 」結曰：「眾人之言不可妄聽，宜依法窮竟。

translations.literal: " Jie said, "The words of the multitude must not be rashly trusted; one should according to law exhaust the case to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jie answered, 'You cannot trust every rumor; investigate to the letter of the law.'

sentences.zh: 」又問僚佐曰：「河北白壤膏粱，何故少人士，每以三品為中正？

translations.literal: " He further asked his staff, "Hebei has white soil and rich fields—why are there few gentlemen, always using third rank as central assessor?
translations.idiomatic: He went on, 'Hebei is fat white farmland—why are there so few eminent families that every third-rank house rates as zhongzheng?'

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「《詩》稱'維嶽降神，生甫及申'。

translations.literal: " They answered, "The 《Book of Odes》 states, 'From the great peak Heaven sent its spirits; it bore Fu and Shen.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone replied, 'The 《Book of Odes》 says Heaven sends its finest spirits down from the sacred peaks.'

sentences.zh: 夫英偉大賢多出於山澤，河北土平氣均，蓬蒿裁高三尺，不足成林故也。

translations.literal: Great heroes and grand worthies mostly come from mountains and marshes; Hebei's earth is level and its qi even, mugwort grows only three feet high—not enough to form a forest—that is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Heroes sprout from rough country; Hebei is flat and tame, its scrub barely shoulder high—no forest, no giants.

sentences.zh: 」結曰：「張彥真以為汝潁巧辯，恐不及青徐儒雅也。

translations.literal: " Jie said, "Zhang Yanzhen thought the Run-Ying sophists could not match the ru elegance of Qing and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jie quoted Zhang Yanzhen: 'The clever talkers of Run and Ying cannot rival the classical scholars of Qing and Xu.'

sentences.zh: 」頵曰：「彥真與元禮不協，故設過言。

translations.literal: " Yun said, "Yanzhen was not on good terms with Yuanli, therefore he set forth excessive words.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yun said, 'Yanzhen feuded with Yuanli—that slander was personal, not geography.'

sentences.zh: 老子、莊周生陳梁，伏羲、傅說、師曠、大項出陽夏，漢魏二祖起於沛譙，准之眾州，莫之與比。

translations.literal: Laozi and Zhuang Zhou were born in Chen and Liang; Fuxi, Fu Yue, Shi Kuang, and great Xiang came from Yangxia; the two founders of Han and Wei rose from Pei and Qiao—measured against the host of provinces, none can compare.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi and Zhuang Zhou were Chen and Liang men; Fuxi, Fu Yue, Shi Kuang, and Xiang Yu hailed from Yangxia; the Han and Wei founders rose in Pei and Qiao—name a province that can match that roll call.

sentences.zh: 」結甚異之，曰：「豫州人士常半天下，此言非虛。

translations.literal: " Jie greatly marveled at him and said, "The gentlemen of Yu Province are always half the realm—this saying is not empty.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jie stared, then said, 'They say half the realm's talent comes from Yuzhou—now I believe it.'

sentences.zh: 」會結遷尚書，結恨不得盡其才用。

translations.literal: " Before long Jie was transferred to minister; Jie regretted that he could not exhaust his employment of Chen's talent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xie Jie went to the ministry in the capital and regretted he had not used Chen Yun to the full.

sentences.zh: 元康中，舉孝廉，而州將留之。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era he was nominated filial and incorrupt, but the provincial commander detained him.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuankang he was put up as filial and incorrupt, but the provincial commander kept him on staff.

sentences.zh: 頵薦同縣焦保曰：「保出自寒素，稟質清沖，若得參嘉命，必能光贊大猷，允清朝望，使黃憲之徒不乏於豫土，令頵庶免臧文之責。

translations.literal: Yun recommended his townsman Jiao Bao, saying, "Bao comes from cold and plain background; endowed nature is clear and pure; if he can join in fine appointment, he will surely be able to brighten and assist the great plan, faithfully clear court expectation, so that men of Huang Xian's sort are not lacking in Yu lands, and I may be spared the blame of Zang Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended his townsman Jiao Bao: 'He is poor but brilliant; give him office and he will honor the court the way Huang Xian once honored his age—then I will not repeat Zang Wenzhong's fault of hiding talent.'

sentences.zh: 」州乃辟保。

translations.literal: " The province thereupon summoned Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The province took Jiao Bao on his word.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏起義，州遣頵將兵赴之，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Jiong raised the righteous army, the province sent Yun to lead troops to join him, and he was appointed commandant-escort.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Jiong, the Prince of Qi, raised the loyalist army, the province sent Chen Yun with troops to join him and named him commandant-escort.

sentences.zh: 遭賊避難於江西。

translations.literal: He encountered bandits and took refuge in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry drove him to take shelter west of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 曆陽內史朱彥引為參軍。

translations.literal: Interior Administrator Zhu Yan of Liyang brought him in as adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yan, interior administrator of Liyang, added him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 鎮東從事中郎袁琇薦頵於元帝，遷鎮東行參軍事，典法兵二曹。

translations.literal: Staff adviser to the east Yuan Xiu recommended Yun to the Yuan Emperor; he was promoted to staff for the campaign east, in charge of the legal and military bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu, staff adviser to the eastern headquarters, introduced him to Yuan of Jin, who made him a campaign staff officer over both law and war bureaus.

sentences.zh: 頵與王導書曰：「中華所以傾弊，四海所以土崩者，正以取才失所，先白望而後實事，浮競驅馳，互相貢薦，言重者先顯，言輕者後敘，遂相波扇，乃至陵遲。

translations.literal: Yun wrote to Wang Dao, saying, "The reason the Central States have collapsed and the four seas have crumbled to earth is precisely that talent has been taken amiss: first empty reputation, then real deeds; float and strife gallop; they mutually push recommendations; those whose words weigh heavily appear first, those whose words weigh lightly are ranked later; thereby wave upon wave, even to decline.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Wang Dao: 'China fell because appointments chased reputations instead of results—men traded favors, loud voices jumped the queue, quiet merit waited, and the whole ladder rotted.'

sentences.zh: 加有莊老之俗傾惑朝廷，養望者為弘雅，政事者為俗人，王職不恤，法物墜喪。
