translations.literal: Add to this the custom of Zhuang and Laozi that overturns and deludes the court: those who cultivate empty reputation are deemed grand and elegant, those who handle government affairs are deemed vulgar men; kingly offices are not cared for, and ritual regalia fall and are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Add the Zhuang-Lao fashion that poisons policy—recluses pass for refined, administrators pass for coarse, offices go empty, and the state's regalia gather dust.'

sentences.zh: 夫欲制遠，先由近始。

translations.literal: If one wishes to regulate what is far, one must begin from what is near.
translations.idiomatic: To rule the horizon you must first fix what lies at your feet.

sentences.zh: 故出其言善，千里應之。

translations.literal: Therefore when one's words go out good, a thousand li respond.
translations.idiomatic: Speak truth at the center and the provinces echo it.

sentences.zh: 今宜改張，明賞信罰，拔卓茂於密縣，顯硃邑於桐鄉，然後大業可舉，中興可冀耳。」

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to change the arrangement, make clear rewards and trustworthy punishments, raise Zhuo Mao from Mi County, display Zhu Yi in Tongxiang—only then can the great enterprise be raised and the restoration be hoped for."
translations.idiomatic: Change course now: spell out rewards and punishments, elevate a Zhuo Mao from obscurity, honor a Zhu Yi in a humble town—then the restoration has a chance.'

sentences.zh: 建興初制，版補錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Under the Jianxing initial regulations he was appointed by tablet as recording secretary on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Jianxing's new rules named him acting recording secretary on the staff.

sentences.zh: 參佐掾屬多設解故以避事任。

translations.literal: Many assistants and subordinates set up excuses of leave to avoid service duties.
translations.idiomatic: Staff men invented leave slips to dodge real work.

sentences.zh: 頵議：「諸僚屬乘昔西台養望餘弊，小心恭肅，更以為俗，偃蹇倨慢，以為優雅。

translations.literal: Yun proposed: "The various subordinates ride on the leftover malpractice of the former western terrace's cultivation of empty reputation: careful respectfulness they take as vulgar; arrogant sloth they take as refined elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yun warned: 'Your aides still mimic the western court's cult of empty fame—diligence looks vulgar to them, swagger looks chic.'

sentences.zh: 至今朝士縱誕，臨事遊行，漸弊不革，以至傾國。

translations.literal: Down to the present court gentlemen give way to wantonness; facing affairs they roam and act; the gradual harm is not reformed, even to overturning the state.
translations.idiomatic: So capital officials grow reckless, drift through assignments, and nobody repairs the rot until the kingdom tips.'

sentences.zh: 故百尋之屋突直而燎焚，千里之堤蟻垤而穿敗，古人防小以全大，慎微以杜萌。

translations.literal: Therefore a house of a hundred xun, if its chimney is straight, is burned by the torch; a dike of a thousand li, if ant mounds pierce it, is broken through; the ancients guarded the small to preserve the large, were careful of the minute to block sprouting.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred-fathom hall burns when the flue runs straight; a thousand-mile levee fails on ant tunnels—the ancients fixed small leaks before the flood.'

sentences.zh: 自今臨使稱疾，須催乃行者，皆免官。」

translations.literal: From now on, if on mission one feigns illness and must be urged before going, all shall be dismissed from office."
translations.idiomatic: From today, any officer who pleads sick on assignment until couriers chase him out the door loses his post.'

sentences.zh: 初，趙王倫篡位，三王起義，制《己亥格》，其後論功雖小，亦皆依用。

translations.literal: At first, when Prince of Zhao Lun usurped the throne, the three princes raised the righteous army and established the 《Yihai Precedent》; afterward, in discussing merit, even small cases all relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun seized the throne, the three princes issued the 《Yihai Precedent》 to rank wartime merit, and later even petty favors hid behind that code.

sentences.zh: 頵意謂不宜以為常式，駁之曰：「聖王懸爵賞功，制罰糾違，斯道苟明，人赴水火。

translations.literal: Yun held that it should not be taken as a constant model and refuted it, saying, "The sage kings suspend ranks to reward merit and institute punishments to correct transgressions—if this way is clear, men will throw themselves into water and fire.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yun argued it must not become permanent law: 'Sage kings reward merit and punish crime—make that clear and men will walk through fire for you.'

sentences.zh: 且名器之實，不可妄假，非才謂之致寇，寵厚戒在斯亡。

translations.literal: Moreover the substance of names and vessels must not be rashly lent; calling the unworthy talented is what brings bandits; the warning that thick favor lies in this perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Titles are not party favors; calling fools worthy invites rebellion; showering empty rank is how dynasties die.'

sentences.zh: 昔孫秀口唱篡逆，手弄天機，惠皇失禦，九服無戴。

translations.literal: Formerly Sun Xiu mouthed usurpation and treason and with his hands played with Heaven's mechanism; Emperor Hui lost the reins, and within the nine domains there was none who wore the cap of loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu preached treason and toyed with the edict; Emperor Hui lost control, and no one in the nine circuits wore the cap straight.'

sentences.zh: 三王建議，席捲四海，合起義之眾，結天下之心，故設《己亥義格》以權濟難。

translations.literal: The three princes set up the plan; they rolled up the four seas; they combined the hosts of the righteous uprising and bound the mind of all under Heaven; therefore they established the 《Yihai Righteousness Precedent》 to weigh and relieve the hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The three princes swept the realm, welded the loyal armies, and issued the 《Yihai Righteousness Precedent》 as a temporary wartime ladder.'

sentences.zh: 此自一切之法，非常倫之格也。

translations.literal: This was in itself a law for all cases, not a norm for ordinary categories.
translations.idiomatic: That was an emergency rulebook, not a peacetime statute.

sentences.zh: 其起義以來，依格雜猥，遭人為侯，或加兵伍，或出皁僕，金紫佩士卒之身，符策委庸隸之門，使天官降辱，王爵黷賤，非所以正皇綱重名器之謂也。

translations.literal: From the uprising onward, according to the precedent it has been mixed and base: persons have been made marquis by pull, some added to the ranks of soldiers, some issued from black servants; gold and purple hang on troopers' persons; tallies and registers lie in menial slaves' gates—this is not what is called rectifying the imperial net and valuing names and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the code has handed marquisates to pull, put silks on privates, and stuffed tally books into lackeys' sleeves—that is not how you mend the net of state or honor a title.'

sentences.zh: 請自今以後宜停之。

translations.literal: I ask that from now on it be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Abolish it from this day forward.

sentences.zh: 」頵以孤寒，數有奏議，朝士多惡之，出除譙郡太守。

translations.literal: " Because Yun was isolated and of cold background, he repeatedly had memorials and proposals; court gentlemen mostly hated him, and he was sent out as grand administrator of Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yun had no faction and a cold pedigree; his blunt papers earned him enemies, and the court parked him as grand administrator of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 大興初，以疾征。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxing he was summoned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daxing he was recalled to the capital on sick leave.

sentences.zh: 久之，白衣兼尚書，因陳時務，以為「昔江外初平，中州荒亂，故貢舉不試。

translations.literal: After a long while, in plain robes he concurrently held the ministry, whereupon he presented the current tasks of the time, holding that "formerly when Jiang wai was first pacified, the central plain was wasteland and turmoil, therefore tribute nomination was not tested.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he served as concurrent minister in plain dress and laid out policy: 'When the south was first pacified and the heartland still a wreck, exams were suspended.'

sentences.zh: 宜漸循舊，搜揚隱逸，試以經策。

translations.literal: It is fitting gradually to follow the old, search and raise the hidden and reclusive, and test them with classics and policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: It is time to phase the old exams back in, call recluses forward, and test them on the canon.'

sentences.zh: 又馬隆、孟觀雖出貧賤，勳濟甚大，以所不習，而統戎事，鮮能以濟。

translations.literal: Moreover Ma Long and Meng Guan, though they came from poverty and lowliness, their merit in saving the age was very great; because what they were not practiced in was commanding military affairs, rarely were they able to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Ma Long and Meng Guan rose from nothing to great deeds, yet war was not their craft and they seldom lasted.'

sentences.zh: 宜開舉武略任將率者，言問核試，盡其所能，然後隨才授任。

translations.literal: It is fitting to open nomination for those with martial strategy fit to be generals and commanders, examine them in speech and question and verify their ability, exhaust what each can do, then according to talent confer appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Open a track for proven tacticians, interview them hard, then match post to gift.'

sentences.zh: 舉十得一，猶勝不舉，況或十得二三。

translations.literal: If in recommending ten you obtain one, it is still better than not recommending—how much more if sometimes you obtain two or three out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Ten recommendations and one hit still beats none—sometimes you will land two or three.'

sentences.zh: 日磾降虜，七世內侍；

translations.literal: Jin Midi was a surrendered barbarian, yet seven generations served within as attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Jin Midi was a captive-turned-councillor whose family served the inner palace for seven generations.

sentences.zh: 由余戎狄，入為秦相。

translations.literal: You Yu was a Rong-Di, yet entered and became Qin minister.
translations.idiomatic: You Yu was a barbarian who became chief minister of Qin.

sentences.zh: 豈藉華宗之族，見齒於奔競之流乎！

translations.literal: How could they rely on splendid lineage clans and be ranked among the rushing-competition crowd!
translations.idiomatic: They did not need gilded pedigrees or a place in the scramble for office.'

sentences.zh: 宜引幽滯之雋，抑華校實，則天清地平，人神感應。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to draw in the outstanding of the secluded and blocked, suppress empty show and verify substance—then Heaven is clear and earth is level, and men and spirits respond to one another."
translations.idiomatic: Lift the buried genius, cut the hollow fame, and Heaven clears, earth steadies, gods and men nod in agreement.'

sentences.zh: 後拜天門太守，殊俗安之。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed grand administrator of Tianmen; the alien customs were pacified by him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as grand administrator of Tianmen, he soothed the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 選腹心之吏為荊州參軍，若有調發，動靜馳白，故恆得宿辦。

translations.literal: He selected heart-and-belly clerks as staff to Jing Province; if there were levies or orders, movements were relayed by swift report, therefore he always had advance preparation overnight.
translations.idiomatic: He planted trusted men on the Jingzhou staff so every levy or movement reached him by fast courier and he could answer overnight.

sentences.zh: 陶侃征還，頵先至巴陵上禮。

translations.literal: When Tao Kan was summoned back, Yun first arrived at Baling to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Kan was recalled, Chen Yun reached Baling first to greet him with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 侃以為能，表為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Kan held him capable and memorialized him as inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan judged him able and recommended him as inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 綏懷荒弊，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: He soothed and cherished the wasteland's exhaustion and had great awe-inspiring kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He nursed a ruined borderland with a mix of awe and mercy.

sentences.zh: 梁州大姓互相嫉妒，說頵年老耳聾，侃召頵還，以西陽太守蔣巽代之。

translations.literal: The great clans of Liang Province mutually envied one another; they slandered Yun as old and deaf; Kan summoned Yun back and replaced him with Jiang Xun as grand administrator of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou's magnates turned on one another and whispered that Chen Yun was old and deaf; Tao Kan recalled him and swapped in Jiang Xun of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 年六十九卒。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 高崧

translations.literal: Section heading: Gao Song.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Song.

sentences.zh: 高崧，字茂琰，廣陵人也。

translations.literal: Gao Song, courtesy name Maoyan, was a native of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Song, courtesy Maoyan, came from Guangling.

sentences.zh: 父悝，少孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: His father Kui in youth was orphaned; he served his mother and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gao Kui lost his parents young and earned a name for tending his mother.

sentences.zh: 年十三，值歲饑，悝菜蔬不饜，每致甘肥於母。

translations.literal: At age thirteen, when it was a year of famine, Kui was not filled with vegetables and coarse food, yet each time he brought sweet fat to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, in a famine year, he went hungry on greens but still set the choicest morsels before his mother.

sentences.zh: 撫幼弟以友愛稱。

translations.literal: He reared his younger brothers and was praised for friendly love.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his younger brothers and was known for fraternal devotion.

sentences.zh: 寓居江州，刺史華軼辟為西曹書佐。

translations.literal: Lodging in Jiang Province, Inspector Hua Yi summoned him as secretary in the western bureau.
translations.idiomatic: While living in Jiangzhou he joined Inspector Hua Yi's staff as western-bureau secretary.

sentences.zh: 及軼敗，悝藏匿軼子經年，會赦乃出。

translations.literal: When Yi was defeated, Kui hid Yi's son for a full year; it was when amnesty was proclaimed that he came out.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Yi fell, Gao Kui hid the boy for a year before bringing him out under amnesty.

sentences.zh: 元帝嘉而宥之，以為參軍，遂曆顯位，至丹陽尹、光祿大夫，封建昌伯。

translations.literal: The Yuan Emperor praised him and pardoned him, appointed him adviser, and he then passed through eminent posts to grand administrator of Danyang, grand master of splendid happiness, and was enfeoffed as count of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan of Jin praised his loyalty, pardoned him, took him on as an adviser, and watched him rise to Danyang governor, grand master of splendid happiness, and count of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 崧少好學，善史書。

translations.literal: Song in youth loved learning and was good at clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Song loved study as a boy and excelled at clerical calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 總角時，司空何充稱其明惠。

translations.literal: When still in hair-knot age, Minister of Works He Chong praised him as bright and clever.
translations.idiomatic: While still a child he won praise from He Chong, the minister of works, for quick wit.

sentences.zh: 充為揚州，引崧為主簿，益相欽重。

translations.literal: When Chong was in Yangzhou, he brought Song in as chief clerk and increasingly honored him.
translations.idiomatic: When He Chong governed Yangzhou he made Gao Song his chief clerk and leaned on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 轉驃騎主簿，舉州秀才，除太學博士，父艱去職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk to the swift cavalry, nominated flourishing talent of the province, appointed erudite of the academy of letters, and left office for father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to chief clerk for the swift cavalry, took provincial flourishing talent, became an academy erudite, then left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 初，悝以納妾致訟被黜，及終，崧乃自系廷尉訟冤，遂停喪五年不葬，表疏數十上。

translations.literal: At first, because Kui had taken a concubine he incurred lawsuit and was demoted; when he died, Song then bound himself and went to the commandant of justice to sue for injustice, whereupon he halted the funeral five years without burial and submitted several tens of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: His father had been cashiered over a concubine suit; when the old man died, Gao Song chained himself to the gate of the commandant of justice to protest the verdict, halted the burial for five years, and filed dozens of appeals.

sentences.zh: 帝哀之，乃下詔曰：「悝備位大臣，違憲被黜，事已久判。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him and thereupon issued an edict saying, "Kui filled a minister's place, violated the statutes and was demoted; the affair was long ago decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity and issued an edict: 'Gao Kui served as a minister, broke the law, and was punished; the case is closed.'

sentences.zh: 其子崧求直無已。

translations.literal: His son Song seeks straight dealing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his son Gao Song will not drop his plea for justice.

sentences.zh: 今特聽傳侯爵。

translations.literal: Now I specially permit transmission of the marquis rank."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore allow him to inherit the marquisate after all.

sentences.zh: 」由是見稱。

translations.literal: Thereby he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: The gesture won him wide praise.

sentences.zh: 拜中書郎、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed gentleman of the palace secretariat and gentleman of the yellow gates.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Song was named a palace-secretariat gentleman and yellow-gates gentleman.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝輔政，引為撫軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen assisted the government, he brought him in as marshal to the army that soothes the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen directed the regency he took Gao Song on as marshal of the pacification army.

sentences.zh: 時桓溫擅威，率眾北伐，軍次武昌，簡文患之。

translations.literal: At the time Huan Wen wielded awesome power, led the hosts on a northern campaign, and the army halted at Wuchang; Jianwen worried over it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen then monopolized military power, marched north, and camped at Wuchang—Jianwen was terrified.

sentences.zh: 崧曰：「宜致書喻以禍福，自當反旆。

translations.literal: Song said, "It is fitting to send a letter explaining fortune and misfortune; of itself he will turn his banners.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Song said, 'Write him a letter that spells out blessing and disaster; he will turn his banners on his own.'

sentences.zh: 如其不爾，便六軍整駕，逆順於茲判矣。

translations.literal: If it is not so, then let the six armies ready the chariots—obedient and rebellious will here be decided.
translations.idiomatic: If he refuses, ready the six hosts—here loyalty and treason will be judged.

sentences.zh: 若有異計，請先釁鼓。

translations.literal: If there are other plans, I ask first to smear the oath drums.
translations.idiomatic: If worse follows, I ask leave to beat the oath drums first.

sentences.zh: 」便於坐為簡文書草曰：「寇難宜平，時會宜接，此實為國遠圖，經略大算。

translations.literal: " Thereupon at his seat he drafted for Jianwen a document saying, "Bandit hardship ought to be pacified; the timely conjunction ought to be met—this is truly the state's long-term plan, the great calculation of strategy.
translations.idiomatic: On the spot he drafted a letter for Jianwen: 'The rebels must be crushed, the moment seized—this is the dynasty's long game.'

sentences.zh: 能弘斯會，非足下而誰！

translations.literal: Who can enlarge this conjunction if not you, sir!
translations.idiomatic: Who but you can seize that moment?

sentences.zh: 但以此興師動眾，要當以資實為本。

translations.literal: But because of this raising the army and moving the masses, fundamentally one must take resources and substance as root.
translations.idiomatic: Yet any campaign lives or dies on money and supplies.

sentences.zh: 運轉之艱，古人之所難，不可易之於始而不熟慮，須所以深用惟疑，在乎此耳。

translations.literal: The hardship of transport and rotation—the ancients found it difficult; it cannot be treated lightly at the beginning without mature consideration—what deeply employs doubt lies in this alone.
translations.idiomatic: Logistics broke ancient armies; do not rush the first move without counting the cost—that is what gives me pause.

sentences.zh: 然異常之舉，眾之所駭，遊聲噂，想足下亦少聞之。

translations.literal: Yet an extraordinary act is what the multitude fears; wandering rumor buzzes; I imagine you, sir, have also scarcely heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: Extraordinary measures frighten the crowd; rumor already flies—I suspect you have heard the whispers too.

sentences.zh: 苟患失之，無所不至。

translations.literal: If one worries about losing (position), there is nothing to which he will not stoop.
translations.idiomatic: Men who fear for their place will stoop to anything.

sentences.zh: 或能望風振擾，一時崩散。

translations.literal: Some may take the wind as signal and stir alarm, in a moment collapse and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Some will panic at rumor and melt away overnight.

sentences.zh: 如其不然者，則望實並喪，社稷之事去矣。

translations.literal: If it is not so, then reputation and substance are both lost, and the business of the altars is gone.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise you lose both credit and substance, and the altars slip from your grasp.

sentences.zh: 皆由吾暗弱，德信不著，不能鎮靜群庶，保固維城，所以內愧於心，外慚良友。

translations.literal: All because I am dim and weak, virtue and trust are not manifest, I cannot quiet the host of commoners or secure the bulwark cities—therefore within I am ashamed in heart, without I blush before good friends.
translations.idiomatic: The fault lies in my own weakness and poor example: I cannot steady the people or shore the fiefs, and I am ashamed before the realm and before you.

sentences.zh: 吾與足下雖職有內外，安社稷，保家國，其致一也。

translations.literal: Although you and I, sir, in office have inner and outer (roles), in securing the altars and protecting house and state our purpose is one.
translations.idiomatic: You serve in the field and I in the chamber, yet we both exist to save the dynasty and the house of Sima.

sentences.zh: 天下安危，系之明德。

translations.literal: The realm's safety and peril hang on enlightened virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's fate rides on your clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 先存甯國，而後圖其外，使王基克隆，大義弘著，所望於足下。

translations.literal: First preserve and quiet the state, afterward plan what lies beyond; cause the royal foundation again to be thick, great righteousness broadly manifest—this is what I hope from you, sir.
translations.idiomatic: Secure the interior before you look outward; thicken the throne's base and let justice show—this is what I beg of you.

sentences.zh: 區區誠懷，豈可復顧嫌而不盡哉！

translations.literal: How can this paltry sincere heart again care for suspicion and not exhaust itself!
translations.idiomatic: How could I hold back honest counsel for fear of giving offense?

sentences.zh: 」溫得書，還鎮。

translations.literal: " When Wen received the letter, he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen read the letter and marched back to his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 崧累遷侍中。

translations.literal: Song was repeatedly promoted to attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Song rose step by step to attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 是時謝萬為豫州都督，疲于親賓相送，方臥在室。

translations.literal: At this time Xie Wan was area commander of Yuzhou, weary from seeing off kin and guests, and was lying down in his chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Wan then commanded Yuzhou, worn out from endless farewell parties, and had taken to his bed.

sentences.zh: 崧徑造之，謂曰：「卿令疆理西籓，何以為政？

translations.literal: Song went straight in to him and said, "You are now to order and govern the western bulwark—by what means will you administer?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Song walked in unannounced and asked, 'You are taking charge of the western marches—what is your plan for governing them?'

sentences.zh: 」萬粗陳其意。

translations.literal: " Wan roughly set forth his idea.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Wan sketched a vague reply.

sentences.zh: 崧便為敘刑政之要數百言。

translations.literal: Song then for him set out the essentials of punishments and administration in several hundred words.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Song then laid out several hundred words on law and administration.

sentences.zh: 萬遂起坐，呼崧小字曰：「阿酃！

translations.literal: Wan thereupon rose from sitting, called Song's childhood name, and said, "A Ling!
translations.idiomatic: Xie Wan sat bolt upright and cried, 'Ah Ling!'

sentences.zh: 故有才具邪！

translations.literal: So you truly have ability and tools!
translations.idiomatic: You really do have the stuff of a statesman!

sentences.zh: 」哀帝雅好服食，崧諫以為「非萬乘所宜。

translations.literal: " Emperor Ai by nature loved taking elixirs; Song remonstrated, holding that "it is not what a rider of ten thousand chariots should do.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai dabbled in elixirs; Gao Song warned that no Son of Heaven should court such risk.

sentences.zh: 陛下此事，實日月之一食也」。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's pursuing this matter is in truth like a single eclipse of the sun and moon."
translations.idiomatic: For a ruler, chasing elixirs is like willing a solar eclipse on yourself.

sentences.zh: 後以公事免，卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed on a public matter and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he lost his post over an administrative matter and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子耆，官至散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His son Qi reached the office of supernumerary gentleman attendant at court.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gao Qi rose to supernumerary gentleman at court.

sentences.zh: 【史論】

translations.literal: Editorial rubric: Historiographer's judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Historian's commentary.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔張良拙說項氏，巧謀於沛公；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In olden times Zhang Liang was clumsy persuading the Xiang house but clever in plotting for the Duke of Pei;
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Zhang Liang could not move Xiang Yu with words, yet he read Liu Bang's mind to perfection;

sentences.zh: 孫惠沮計齊王，耀奇於東海，終而誓甘之旅炎運載昌，稱狩之師金行不競。

translations.literal: Sun Hui thwarted the Prince of Qi's plan and displayed strange stratagem to the Prince of the Eastern Sea, yet in the end the hosts that swore the sweet pledge saw the fiery fortune ride to glory, while the armies that styled themselves on the imperial hunt could not make the metal line prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui checked Sima Jiong yet dazzled Sima Yue; still, the loyalist oaths that fired Western Jin could not repeat Han's blazing rise, and the great hosts that marched under the hunt banner never secured the metal mandate of Sima Jin.

sentences.zh: 豈遭時之會斯蹇，將謀國之道未通？

translations.literal: Was it that meeting the times' conjunction was this hard, or the way of plotting for the state was not thorough?
translations.idiomatic: Was the hour itself unkind, or did their statecraft never quite measure up?

sentences.zh: 迷於委質之貞，暗于所修之慮，本既顛矣，何以能終！

translations.literal: Lost in the fidelity of surrendering allegiance, blind in the considerations of what they cultivated—once the root is overturned, how can they reach the end!
translations.idiomatic: They mistook personal loyalty for policy and misread what truly needed tending—uproot a tree and it cannot stand long.

sentences.zh: 熊遠、王鑒有毗濟之道，比之大廈，其榱桷之佐乎！

translations.literal: Xiong Yuan and Wang Jian had the way of aiding and sustaining; compared to a great hall, were they perhaps the rafter-end assistants!
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan and Wang Jian were the men who steadied the timbers—never the central pillar, yet without their braces the hall would have fallen.

sentences.zh: 崧之詆溫，頵之距結，挫其勞役之策，申其汝潁之論，采郭嘉之風旨，挹硃育之餘波，故桓溫輟許攸之謀，解結欽王朗之跡。

translations.literal: Song's rebuke of Wen, Yun's resistance to Jie—frustrated their schemes of forced labor, set forth the Run-Ying thesis, sampled Guo Jia's intent, scooped Zhu Yu's after-ripples—therefore Huan Wen set aside a Xun You-style plot, and Xie Jie looked up to Wang Lang's traces.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Song's letter to Huan Wen and Chen Yun's stand against Xie Jie broke reckless mobilization, revived the Run-Ying argument, echoed Guo Jia's bluntness and Zhu Yu's wit—so Huan Wen dropped a rash Xun You scheme and Xie Jie learned to admire Wang Lang's example.

sentences.zh: 緝之時典，用此道歟！

translations.literal: As for Xiong Jin's timely norms in office—did he employ this same way!
translations.idiomatic: Even Xiong Jin's later service seems to have walked the same path.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：臨湘遊藝，才識英發。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: Linxiang roamed the arts; talent and judgment shone bright.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: The Linxiang lord mastered letters and strategy, his genius plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 詭名違穎，陳書幹越。

translations.literal: With false name he fled Ying; he presented a letter to lobby Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He fled Chengdu under an alias and moved Sima Yue with his pen.

sentences.zh: 孝文忠謇，嘉言斯踐。

translations.literal: Xiaowen was loyal and forthright; fine words were thus put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan the 'filial and literate' lived blunt loyalty—his good counsel was heeded.

sentences.zh: 茂高器鑒，雕章尤善。

translations.literal: Maogao had vessel and discernment; carved writings he was especially good at.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian the 'luxuriant and lofty' read men and texts with equal sharpness.

sentences.zh: 侯爵崧傳，高門頵顯。

translations.literal: The marquis rank passed down in Song's biography; the lofty gate made Yun illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Song's marquisate endured in the record; Chen Yun's house rose to lasting fame.
